intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding myelin protein zero (MPZ).

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy-2 (CHN2) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding myelin protein zero (MPZ).
checks.evidence_quote: the identification of a mutation in the gene (MPZ) for protein zero (P0) associated with this phenotype are described.
checks.explanation: The abstract links an MPZ mutation to congenital hypomyelination (CH). It does not say the mutation is heterozygous or use the CHN2 designation.

paragraphs.text: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare, severe hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy with prenatal, neonatal, or early infantile onset of hypotonia, distal muscle weakness, and areflexia, with severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities (Mandich et al., 1999; Smit et al., 2008). Nerve biopsy shows absent or thin myelin sheaths (Smit et al., 2008). Smit et al. (2008) noted that most of the few patients described in the literature died within the first years of life.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a rare, severe hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Congenital hypomyelination (CH) is a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy. It does not describe it as 'rare' or 'severe' (it only mentions severe slowing of conduction velocities).

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy has prenatal, neonatal, or early infantile onset.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by prenatal, neonatal or early infantile onset of hypotonia, paresis and areflexia

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy presents with hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by early infancy onset, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities
checks.explanation: Hypotonia is listed as a feature.

checks.evidence_quote: characterized by early infancy onset, distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia
checks.explanation: Distal muscle weakness is listed as a feature.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy presents with areflexia.
checks.evidence_quote: distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities
checks.explanation: Areflexia is listed as a feature.

checks.claim: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy shows severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities.
checks.evidence_quote: areflexia, and severe slowing of nerve conduction velocities

checks.evidence_quote: Histopathologically there are no or thin myelin sheaths.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this as a histopathological finding, which matches the nerve biopsy claim.

checks.claim: Most of the few patients with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy described in the literature died within the first years of life.
checks.evidence_quote: Most of the few patients described in literature die within the first years of life.

paragraphs.text: Mandich et al. (1999) described the clinical, morphologic, and immunohistochemical features of a patient with congenital hypomyelination. The clinical features were considered quite distinct from those of the more frequent Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B or Dejerine-Sottas syndrome.

checks.evidence_quote: the clinical, morphological, and immunohistochemical features of a CH case

checks.evidence_quote: a patient presenting with clinical features quite distinct from those of the more frequent Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 1B disease (CMT1B) or Dejerine-Sottas syndrome (DSS)

checks.explanation: The abstract calls CMT1B and DSS 'more frequent'.

paragraphs.text: Szigeti et al. (2003) reported a patient with congenital hypomyelination associated with cranial nerve dysfunction, respiratory failure, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, which confounded the clinical picture. Muscle biopsy findings suggested an effect of abnormal innervation on early postnatal muscle fiber differentiation.

checks.explanation: The draft's 'suggested' is a fair paraphrase of the abstract's 'allude to'.

paragraphs.text: Kochanski et al. (2004) described the clinical and morphologic features of a patient with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy. They noted that sural nerve biopsy in this disorder characteristically shows nonmyelinated and poorly myelinated axons with basal lamina onion bulbs and lack of myelin breakdown products.

paragraphs.text: Smit et al. (2008) reported a long-term follow-up study of a family with congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy affecting 2 generations.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous MPZ mutations in the patients reported by Mandich et al. (1999) and Szigeti et al. (2003) occurred de novo. Smit et al. (2008) confirmed a heterozygous MPZ mutation in 2 generations of a family, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Warner et al. (1996) identified 5 novel mutations in the MPZ gene in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B, Dejerine-Sottas syndrome, or congenital hypomyelination. They suggested that these disorders represent a spectrum of related myelinopathies, and hypothesized that differences in clinical severity are related to the type of mutation and its effect on protein function (loss of function versus dominant negative).

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) identified 5 novel mutations in the MPZ gene in patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B, Dejerine-Sottas syndrome, or congenital hypomyelination.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified five novel mutations in the myelin protein zero (MPZ) gene, encoding the major structural protein (P0) of peripheral nerve myelin, in patients with either CMT1B, DSS, or CH.

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) suggested that Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B, Dejerine-Sottas syndrome, and congenital hypomyelination represent a spectrum of related myelinopathies.
checks.evidence_quote: This finding suggests that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities, but rather represent a spectrum of related "myelinopathies" due to an underlying defect in myelination.

checks.claim: Warner et al. (1996) hypothesized that differences in clinical severity among MPZ-related myelinopathies are related to the type of mutation and its effect on protein function (loss of function versus dominant negative).
checks.evidence_quote: we hypothesize the differences in clinical severity seen with mutations in MPZ are related to the type of mutation and its subsequent effect on protein function (i.e., loss of function versus dominant negative).

paragraphs.text: In a patient with congenital hypomyelination, Mandich et al. (1999) identified a de novo gln215-to-ter (Q215X) mutation in the MPZ gene, confirming that congenital hypomyelination is allelic with disorders of less severe phenotype.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with congenital hypomyelination, Szigeti et al. (2003) identified a complex de novo mutation in the MPZ gene, consisting of a 3-bp deletion (CTA) of nucleotides 550 to 552 and insertion of a G at nucleotide 550, predicted to result in a frameshift.

checks.claim: Szigeti et al. (2003) identified a complex mutation in the MPZ gene in a patient with congenital hypomyelination, consisting of a 3-bp deletion (CTA) of nucleotides 550 to 552 and insertion of a G at nucleotide 550.
checks.evidence_quote: a complex de novo myelin protein zero (MPZ) mutation consisting of a 3bp deletion of CTA from nucleotide 550 to 552 and insertion of G at nucleotide 550
checks.explanation: The mutation matches the abstract exactly. The verdict is partial only because the abstract says 'a case of congenital hypomyelination' (a phenotype with cranial nerve, respiratory and cardiac involvement) and never names congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy. 'A patient with congenital hypomyelination' is therefore a close but not literal restatement. Only the abstract was available.

checks.explanation: The abstract states the mutation is de novo.

agent.process_note: All 5 papers are available as abstracts only, and I read every one in full. None of the abstracts gives patient ages, ancestry, consanguinity, cDNA numbering in HGVS form, or functional data. Warner et al. (1996) does not say which of its 5 MPZ mutations occurred in congenital hypomyelination, and Smit et al. (2008) does not name the MPZ mutation in its family, so neither became an allelic variant. No reference data was supplied, so the intro leaves out the MIM number and chromosome location for MPZ.
